claims.text: Wear performance of high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is governed by synergy between nanocrystalline strengthening and formation of a protective oxide layer.
As-deposited high-entropy-alloy coatings can have a nanocrystalline BCC structure.
The relevant as-deposited coatings may instead have a dual-phase structure.
As-deposited coatings have moderate surface roughness and minimal oxide coverage.
Post-deposition annealing at approximately 300 °C is applicable to a nanocrystalline CuMoTaWV high-entropy-alloy coating.
Post-deposition annealing further refines the coating microstructure by decreasing its grain size.
Post-deposition annealing promotes formation of a uniform, adherent protective oxide layer, such as CuO or spinel-type oxide.
Decreasing nanocrystalline grain size increases coating hardness through grain-boundary strengthening.
A uniform protective oxide film minimizes direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding and thereby reduces friction and wear.
The balance between grain-boundary strengthening and oxide-film protection governs overall tribological performance.
Annealing will increase coating hardness relative to the as-deposited state.
Annealing will improve coating adhesion relative to the as-deposited state.
Annealed coatings will have a lower wear rate than as-deposited coatings, particularly at room temperature.
Annealed coatings will have a lower coefficient of friction than as-deposited coatings.
Elevated-temperature oxide formation will further reduce wear.
The coefficient of friction may increase at elevated temperature if the oxide layer transforms tribochemically.
The as-deposited baseline has a coarser grain structure, higher roughness, and less protective oxide formation than the annealed coating.
A coating thickness of approximately 900 nm is representative of the proposed applicability range.
The mechanism should apply to refractory or equimolar high-entropy-alloy coatings that form beneficial oxides during moderate annealing.
The mechanism may fail when an alloy forms non-protective or overly abrasive oxides.
